evals.prompt: Inspect our live AWS network routing topology in ap-south-1 (VPCs, route tables, Transit Gateways, Cloud WAN Core Networks, and VPN connections) in read-only mode, report what currently exists honestly, and explain the 'two-lookup' forwarding model when traffic flows from a VPC through a Transit Gateway or Cloud WAN Core Network Edge (CNE) to a Direct Connect Gateway (DXGW) and on-premises VIF.

expectations: Activates the aws-routing skill and inspects ap-south-1 VPCs, Transit Gateways, Cloud WAN Core Networks, and VPN connections via connected MCP tools (`awsnetwork` and/or `aws-mcp`) without running raw `aws` CLI shell commands

evals.prompt: Our enterprise has a global Direct Connect Gateway (`dxgw-global`) with one Transit VIF in `ap-south-1` (Mumbai) and one Transit VIF in `eu-west-1` (Ireland), both advertising `10.50.0.0/16` to AWS. During maintenance in Mumbai, our network engineer prepended the AS_PATH 5 times (`65001 65001 65001 65001 65001`) on the Mumbai VIF expecting `ap-south-1` VPC traffic to shift over to the Ireland VIF (`65001`), yet `ap-south-1` traffic is STILL exiting via the Mumbai VIF! Explain step-by-step why AS-path prepending failed and what exact BGP mechanism steers `ap-south-1` egress across regions.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-routing, names the DXGW selection lookup, explains that DXGW evaluates Longest Prefix Match -> Local Preference -> AS_PATH length -> MED (stopping at the first differing attribute), shows that DXGW automatically assigns higher default Local Preference (`7224:7200` medium) to a local associated-Region DX connection over a remote Region so AS_PATH prepending is never consulted, and prescribes explicit DX BGP local-preference communities (`7224:7100` Low on Mumbai and `7224:7300` High on Ireland) which override default local-region LP, plus checking the connection's associated Region via `describe-connections`.
expectations: Activates the aws-routing skill and names the Direct Connect Gateway (DXGW) BGP path-selection stage

Explains the exact DXGW evaluation order (Longest Prefix Match -> Local Preference -> AS_PATH length -> MED) and why AS-path prepending failed: DXGW applies a higher default Local Preference to a local associated-Region DX VIF than to a remote-Region VIF, stopping selection before AS_PATH is ever compared

Prescribes using AWS Direct Connect Local Preference BGP communities (`7224:7300` High, `7224:7200` Medium, `7224:7100` Low) to steer cross-region egress deterministically, and warns to verify the connection's associated Region (`describe-connections`) at multi-Region DX locations

evals.prompt: We are migrating from AWS Transit Gateway to **AWS Cloud WAN** and attaching three separate Direct Connect Gateways (one per data center: ASNs `65010`, `65011`, `65012`), each advertising all three data-center `/16` prefixes into Cloud WAN. Walk through the exact Cloud WAN Core Network Edge (CNE) route evaluation order, explain how Cloud WAN differs from Transit Gateway when multiple DXGWs are attached, and explain how to steer traffic deterministically between the three DXGWs (including the BGP community limitation on Cloud WAN DX attachments).
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-routing, details the per-CNE Cloud WAN evaluation order (Longest Prefix Match -> Static -> System 1:1 NAT -> same-region VPC-propagated -> Dynamic routes: CNE routing-policy `set-local-preference` default 0 -> shortest AS_PATH -> lowest MED -> source preference: DXGW > Cloud WAN Connect > S2S VPN > remote CNE/TGW peering deterministically random per segment), contrasts multi-DXGW on Cloud WAN (CNE evaluates each DXGW attachment independently; without policy, identical routes are non-deterministic) vs TGW, prescribes Cloud WAN Routing Policies (version `2025.11+` inbound `set-local-preference` 300/200/100 matched via `prefix-in-cidr` / `prefix-in-prefix-list`), and warns BGP communities cannot be matched/set on DX attachments in Cloud WAN.
expectations: Activates the aws-routing skill and states the Cloud WAN per-CNE route evaluation order: Longest Prefix Match -> Static -> System (1:1 NAT) -> VPC-propagated (same region) -> Dynamic (`set-local-preference` higher wins -> shortest AS_PATH -> lowest MED) -> Source preference (DXGW > Connect > S2S VPN > remote CNE/TGW peering)
Contrasts multiple DXGW attachments on Cloud WAN (where the CNE evaluates routes from each DXGW attachment itself, yielding non-deterministic selection without a policy) against Transit Gateway

Prescribes inbound **Cloud WAN Routing Policies** (policy version `2025.11+`, using `set-local-preference`, `prepend-asn-list`, or `set-med` matched by `prefix-in-cidr` or `prefix-in-prefix-list`), explicitly noting that BGP communities cannot be matched or set on Direct Connect attachments in Cloud WAN and mentioning RIB (`list-core-network-routing-information`) vs installed Routes verification

evals.prompt: On our AWS Transit Gateway (`tgw-prod`), we have a 10 Gbps Direct Connect Gateway attachment dynamically advertising `10.0.0.0/8` and `10.10.0.0/16` via BGP, and we also added a backup Site-to-Site VPN attachment configured with **static routing** for `10.10.0.0/16` and `10.10.5.0/24`. Our monitoring shows 100% of production traffic to `10.10.0.0/16` and `10.10.5.0/24` is saturating the 1.25 Gbps VPN tunnel instead of using the 10 Gbps Direct Connect link! Explain why at the TGW route table and compare deterministic ways to fix active/passive DX + VPN backup.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-routing, names the Transit Gateway route table lookup, explains two distinct reasons: (1) for `10.10.5.0/24`, Longest Prefix Match (`/24` beats `/16` and `/8`) wins before any attachment/protocol comparison, and (2) for identical `10.10.0.0/16`, **static routes on TGW have higher priority than dynamic Direct Connect BGP-propagated routes**, so static VPN wins over DX! Recommends converting the backup VPN to dynamic **BGP routing** with identical prefix lengths (`10.10.0.0/16` on both DX and BGP VPN, where TGW prefers DXGW over BGP VPN) or isolating backup routes, and warns against asymmetric return routing from on-prem.
expectations: Activates the aws-routing skill and names the Transit Gateway route table evaluation

Identifies both causes: `10.10.5.0/24` wins via **Longest Prefix Match** (`/24` > `/16`), and for equal prefix `10.10.0.0/16` **static TGW routes outrank dynamic Direct Connect BGP-propagated routes**

Recommends switching the backup Site-to-Site VPN from static routing to **dynamic BGP routing** advertising matching prefix lengths (so TGW's attachment/origin preference naturally prefers Direct Connect over BGP VPN while avoiding ECMP across mismatched attachment types) and ensuring symmetric on-premises return routing

evals.prompt: Our network team created two separate Direct Connect Gateways (`dxgw-1` with `amazonSideAsn: 64512` and `dxgw-2` with `amazonSideAsn: 64513`) attached to the same Transit Gateway to achieve active-active ECMP across two 10G Transit VIFs (`ASN 65100` and `ASN 65200`), but `search-transit-gateway-routes` only installs one DXGW attachment as next hop! Explain why ECMP is an outcome rather than a step, list every broken condition preventing ECMP here, and recommend the canonical architecture.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-routing, states 'ECMP is an outcome, not a step' (occurring only when prefix length, LP, AS_PATH, and MED all tie), identifies why cross-DXGW ECMP failed on TGW: (1) different customer ASNs (`65100` vs `65200` — Multipath AS-Path Relax is unsupported; exact same ASNs required), and (2) mismatched DXGW `amazonSideAsn` (`64512` vs `64513` — must match for cross-DXGW TGW ECMP!), warns that non-qualifying tied DXGWs pick a single winner non-deterministically, and recommends using **one single DXGW with multiple Transit VIFs** (same ASN/equal attributes) where DXGW performs ECMP natively.
expectations: Activates the aws-routing skill and explains that **ECMP is an outcome, not a step** in route evaluation

Identifies both blockers to cross-DXGW ECMP on Transit Gateway: different on-premises ASNs (`65100` vs `65200` — BGP Multipath AS-Path Relax is not supported; exact AS_PATH match required) AND different DXGW `amazonSideAsn` values (`64512` vs `64513`)

Recommends the canonical AWS pattern: consolidating onto **a single Direct Connect Gateway with multiple Transit VIFs** (equal LP, AS_PATH, and MED) for deterministic ECMP, and provides read-only validation commands (`search-transit-gateway-routes`, `list-virtual-interface-routes`, `describe-direct-connect-gateways`)

Which next hop does the VPC route table select for: (a) an S3 IP in `ap-south-1` (`52.219.64.10`), (b) an S3 IP in `us-east-1`, and (c) `10.20.5.12` if someone tries to add a `/24` more-specific subnet route to an inspection appliance ENI (`10.20.5.0/24 -> eni-fw`)?
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-routing, evaluates the VPC subnet route table step-by-step: (a) `ap-south-1` S3 IP matches `pl-68a54001` (AWS-managed S3 prefix list is more specific than `0.0.0.0/0`) -> routes to `vpce-0123`; (b) `us-east-1` S3 IP is not in `ap-south-1`'s S3 prefix list -> falls through to `0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0abc`; and (c) explains VPC Local Route More-Specific Routing (`10.20.5.0/24 -> eni-fw` matching a subnet CIDR within the VPC beats the `/16` `local` route when routing between subnets via a middlebox ENI/GWLB endpoint).

Traces (a) `ap-south-1` S3 IP matching the more-specific S3 prefix list `pl-*` -> `vpce-0123` vs (b) `us-east-1` S3 IP missing the regional `pl-*` -> falling back to `0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0abc`

Explains (c) VPC more-specific subnet routing: a `/24` route matching a subnet's exact CIDR pointing to an inspection appliance ENI / GWLB endpoint overrides the `/16` `local` route by longest-prefix match

evals.prompt: Our on-premises firewall is dropping TCP sessions between on-premises servers and our AWS VPCs in ap-south-1 with 'TCP SYN-ACK without matching SYN' state errors! We run an active Private VIF (`dxvif-main`) plus a BGP Site-to-Site VPN on the same Virtual Private Gateway (VGW), and our on-prem router was configured with a local-preference of `200` preferring the VPN tunnel outbound (`on-prem -> AWS`) while leaving inbound DX BGP advertisements untouched. Trace the forward and return paths across every route table and show how to make routing symmetric.
evals.expected_output: Activates aws-routing, traces both directions: `on-prem -> AWS` (ingress) is controlled by the customer router's higher Local Preference (`200`), sending TCP SYN over the VPN tunnel; `AWS -> on-prem` (egress) is evaluated independently by VGW/AWS route selection, which prefers Direct Connect VIF over BGP VPN for identical prefix lengths, sending SYN-ACK back over `dxvif-main` and bypassing the stateful VPN firewall! Recommends aligning both directions (customer router LP/weight/MED for ingress + matching prefix lengths/LP communities for egress, or stateful firewall ECMP/zone grouping).
expectations: Activates the aws-routing skill and traces the end-to-end forward (`on-prem -> AWS` over VPN) and return (`AWS -> on-prem` over Direct Connect VIF) paths to explain the stateful firewall TCP drop

Clearly distinguishes directional control levers: **on-prem -> AWS (ingress)** is controlled by the customer router's local-preference/weight, whereas **AWS -> on-prem (egress)** is controlled by VGW/DXGW route evaluation (which prefers Direct Connect over BGP VPN at equal prefix length)

Provides symmetric remediation options (preferring Direct Connect outbound on the customer router so both directions use DX with VPN as standby, or advertising a more-specific/AS-prepended/LP-aligned policy symmetrically) plus read-only validation commands

evals.prompt: Traffic from our European VPCs is 'going to the wrong Direct Connect location in London'—we have a 10 Gbps port at Equinix LD5 (Slough) and another port at Telehouse West, and we use Cloud WAN. evals.expected_output: Activates aws-routing, highlights the dual-Region Direct Connect location gotcha on **Equinix LD5 (Slough)**: 1G and 10G ports at LD5 can terminate on devices associated with **either `eu-west-1` (Ireland) OR `eu-west-2` (London)** (whereas Telehouse West is `eu-west-2` London), so a 10G LD5 connection associated with `eu-west-1` is treated by the `eu-west-2` CNE/DXGW as *remote*! Lists the strategic discovery checks (`directconnect describe-connections` `region`, `list-virtual-interface-routes` LP communities/AS_PATH, single vs multiple DXGWs, and Cloud WAN RIB vs Routes).
expectations: Activates the aws-routing skill

Explains the multi-Region Direct Connect location behavior at **Equinix LD5 (Slough)**: 1G/10G connections at LD5 can be associated with either `eu-west-1` (Ireland) or `eu-west-2` (London) depending on the terminating AWS device, which determines whether DXGW treats the VIF as local (`7224:7200`) or remote for a London CNE

Provides the exact read-only confirmation checks (`directconnect describe-connections` to verify associated `region`, `list-virtual-interface-routes` for LP communities/AS_PATH, and Cloud WAN `get-network-routes` / `list-core-network-routing-information`)
